turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_zt400_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (Sb, O, Te, Mg, Se, Co, Sn, Pb, S, Si, Cu, Ni, Ge, Bi, Ti, Fe,
    Zn, Zr, In, Ca, Ag) and `target` (the measured zT (thermoelectric figure
    of merit) at 400 K).
  - b3_te_zt400_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT (thermoelectric
    figure of merit) at 400 K was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT
(thermoelectric figure of merit) at 400 K, then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training set shows that the highest measured zT(400 K) values cluster in a small number of composition families (nearest-neighbor inspection of the top ~15 points):

- Mg–Sb–Bi (zT \(\approx 0.79\))
- off-stoichiometric PbTe (zT \(\approx 0.78\))
- Sn-rich (zT \(\approx 0.71\))
- Mg\(_2\)(Si,Sn) solid solutions, especially Sn-rich or lightly Sb-doped (zT \(0.55\)–\(0.65\))

All other families (CoSb\(_3\) skutterudites, GeTe, PbSe, half-Heuslers, oxides, \ldots) top out well below 0.45.

Direct composition matching of the 100-candidate pool against these families yields five clear analogues, ranked by the zT of their nearest training neighbours:

- c043 is essentially identical to the 0.79 Mg–Sb–Bi point (only a 2 at.% Co difference).
- c037 is the 0.45/0.50 PbTe composition that produced 0.78.
- c010 reproduces the Sn-rich point that produced 0.71.
- c049 lies inside the Mg\(_2\)Si–Sn cluster (closest neighbour 0.57, another neighbour 0.65).
- c046 is the most Sn-rich Mg\(_2\)(Si,Sn) candidate (nearest neighbours 0.55–0.66).

No other pool entry is closer to any training point above 0.50.

Final: c043, c037, c010, c049, c046
